name: Shebna
title: The Steward Who Was Removed
summary: Shebna was a high-ranking official under King Hezekiah of Judah, serving as steward (palace administrator). He was condemned by the prophet Isaiah for his pride and self-exaltation, especially for carving out an elaborate tomb in the rock. He was later demoted from his position as steward to scribe and replaced by Eliakim, son of Hilkiah.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Judgment Against Shebna
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah prophesied against Shebna for his pride and for carving out a magnificent tomb in the rock, declaring that the Lord would cast him away.

keyEvents.title: Eliakim Appointed in Shebna's Place
keyEvents.description: God declared through Isaiah that Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, would take over Shebna's position as steward and receive the key to the house of David.

keyEvents.title: Shebna as Scribe During the Assyrian King's Threat
keyEvents.description: During Sennacherib's siege of Jerusalem, Shebna was sent out as scribe along with Eliakim and Joah to meet the Assyrian Rabshakeh outside the walls of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The delegation brings a message to Hezekiah
keyEvents.description: After hearing the threatening speech of the Rabshakeh, Eliakim, Shebna and Joah tore their clothes and brought the message to King Hezekiah.

keyEvents.title: Sent to the prophet Isaiah
keyEvents.description: King Hezekiah sent Eliakim, Shebna the scribe and the elders among the priests to the prophet Isaiah to ask for prayer when Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in Isaiah
keyEvents.description: The same event involving the Assyrian threat and the delegation that included Shebna is also described in the book of Isaiah.
